messages.subject: Multiple Constraints on a Parameter
parts:
Hello,

I am attempting to run a simple confirmatory factor analysis in stan with ordered categorical outcomes.  I am using a latent parameterization with cutpoints for the underlying normally distributed variable.  The problem is that my matrix of parameters (my latents) is declared as real, but my distribution for y is truncated...

  matrix[N,7] y;

    for (j in 1:7) { 
      y[i,j]~normal(mu[i,j], sqrt(psi[j])) T[thresh[j,z[i,j]],thresh[j,z[i,j]+1]];
    }

The problem, of course, is the inconsistency of declaration.  So I'm wondering if there is any way to declare lower and upper bounds for elements of this y matrix that differ from one another?  I know by looking at other threads it wasn't possible a couple of years ago, but is it now?  Andrew Gelman has stan code for an ARM example (17.6)  where he declares a truncated distribution but doesn't have appropriate bounds in the parameter block.  So I'm wondering how that would work?  Any suggestions?  It's similar to multilevel ordered categorical regression; the truncation is dependent on cutpoints.  The only difference I can see is that my cutpoints are fixed and Gelman's are random. 

Thanks for any help on this, 

Darcie Delzell

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Multiple Constraints on a Parameter
parts:
If y is data, there's no problem (we use y for
modeled data, x for predictors and greek letters for
parameters).

If it's a parameter, the only way to deal with it for
the moment is to declare the parameters as unconstrained
then constrain them yourself---the transform and required
Jacobian is listed in the "Transformations of Constrained
Variables" chapter of the manual.

- Bob
